chapter: Three Deuces and 52nd Street with Tatum
title: Sitting in with the Tatum trio
summary: Almost nobody sat in with Tatum except Buddy Rich; he also recalls no outsiders at Lovejoy's.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Did other musicians sit in with you while you were playing there?

Yeah, I met Charlie Parker through that same sittin' in process. Very few people like it when you got your own group and you all been playing every night and you get your set routines and things. When somebody sits in that automatically makes it a jam session. But this particular night this fellow came in, I had never seen him before...
Charlie Parker? before we get into that I wanted to ask you if people sat in much with the Tatum trio.

No, there really wasn't no takers, in a way of speaking. Because they knew if they got in there, he didn't play around. I said, the only fellow that ever sat in with us that I know of was Buddy Rich. He played drums. There was no other -- I don't even remember Oscar Moore sittin' in. And he was one of the greatest guitar players around at that particular time. But he was with the King Cole trio.
Did other people play at the jams in Lovejoy's in California?
No, not that I can remember. I don't even remember one. Maybe, whoever was out there, like Ben Webster or somebody may have come in and played, but I don't remember. We did the whole thing ourselves,
And we were drawing people with the turnovers, and getting nothing but a chicken leg and a drink.
